explanation: Fires on the word right after a verb or noun describing physical location or state (waited, sat, stood, lurk, found, stored), most often 'in' as in 'waited in line', 'stood in the', 'was in full swing'. It also fires on the next slot of fixed phrases like 'in perfect condition', 'in hot pursuit', 'got off the ground'. Other prepositions and words after 'in' fire more weakly.

Fires on word pieces in the middle or end of technical or specialized terms: programming words (Xcode, typescript, template <class/typename>, monads, directive), biochemistry suffixes (prostaglandin, synovial, reticulum, phenylalanine, encodes) and parts of legal captions (ATTORNEY FOR, P.A., representatives of). Ordinary prose words fire weakly. No single shared concept is clear.

Mixed. It fires strongly on sentence-opening words that come right after a period or newline (' In', '.In', ' For', ' This') in Q&A, technical or code-heavy text. It also fires on pieces of technical identifiers and terms (KEYPOINT, data volume, prion, recombination, valgus, ' init'). Function words inside ordinary prose fire weakly.

Fires on internal subword pieces of long scientific or technical compound words, especially analytical chemistry and biochemistry terms (spectrometry/'rom', fluoroquinolone/'quin', Raman, caspase, proteoglycan, perovskite) and chip names like STM32/CV_32 (the '3'). Ordinary English words fire only weakly.

Fires on non-initial subword pieces of names, abbreviations and acronyms in parentheses (PUF, Hcy, EDDP, SSSI, CLEVELAND, MACY, Hereford, Robbins). It also fires on the possessive in 'one's', and on 'of' or 'group' that finishes a set phrase (train of thought, tug-of-war, age group). The core idea is completing a multi-token name or fixed expression.

Mostly fires on function words in fixed, formulaic frames: 'to' after 'possible'/'need'/'wishing', 'which' in 'by which', 'the' in 'Licensed to the', and the comma in thousands-separated numbers or after a year (753, 201; 2019, an). 'the edge' in 'living life on the edge' is the top case. Most activations are moderate.

Fires on a token that is or starts with the letter 'P'/'p' at the start of a word, especially a capital P beginning a name, word or sentence (Pichia, Paphos, Pulmonary, Puzzle, iPads, .p in URLs). Mid-word 'p' and pieces like 'ap' or '_P' fire moderately. Whole common words starting with p (piano, poll) fire weakly.

Mixed set of specific words: 'view' (please view the LICENSE, in full view), 'ostensibly'/'seemingly', 'rigid'/'rig', 'complex', 'from' after 'stop X', plus scattered adjectives (alien, exotic, conditioning). No clear unifying context.

Fires on closing punctuation that ends a bracketed or quoted span, mostly ')' (and ')-', '-)') closing a parenthetical inside running text, as in '(non-)degenerate', '(or decrease)', '(PK)-resistant'. It also fires on closing braces '}}', generic closers '>>', and closing quotes or emphasis marks. Opening brackets do not fire it.

Mixed. It fires on words in software license and copyright boilerplate ('rights' in 'All rights reserved'/'limitation the rights', 'permissions', 'You should'). It also fires on the closing '*/' or '*)' of boxed comment-header lines, and on 'up' in 'opened up'. Assorted other words fire as well.

Fires on a verb or word right after a subject, auxiliary or modal in informal narrative, often in phrasal verbs ('pop it in', 'turned out', 'head on over', 'sit down', 'go to work', 'went with'). It also fires on 'or' in boilerplate ('No such file or directory', 'Software or'). The activations are broad and diffuse.

No coherent pattern. It fires on commas after title-like noun phrases at the start of a text ('Signal transduction inhibitors,'), on 'from' after 'surge', on 'end' in 'since the end of', and on various subword pieces, numbers and adverbs.

Fires on punctuation and operator tokens that join parts inside code, URLs or markup: member-access dots and '?.', '::', '=' in query strings, '://', '#', '@', '</' of closing XML tags, '(' and '))'. Similar punctuation in ordinary prose fires weakly.

Fires on the first subword piece of words in non-English or foreign-name text: Italian, French, Finnish, Norwegian, Hungarian words and Indian, Italian or Portuguese surnames and place names split into pieces (' Ch'awla, ' F'iumicino, ' Fi'orentino). It also fires on CJK characters and French apostrophes ('d''envoi). English words fire weakly.

Mixed. It fires on 'license' in 'contributor license agreements' and on 'of'/'in' in license boilerplate ('list of conditions', 'distributed in the hope'). It also fires on 'few' after 'a', as in 'a few pixels/millimeters', and on number or size words before a unit (million, ter-abytes). 'and' in 'rows and columns' fires too.
No clear theme. It fires on assorted function words and pieces in technical or Q&A text: 'and', 'or', 'of', ''t' in 'doesn't/didn't', 'first', '(' after a name, 'process', 'jest'.

Fires on the infinitive 'to' expressing purpose right after 'used'/'use(s) X', as in 'was used to estimate', 'can be used to', 'used it to spy'. Purpose 'to' after other verbs (uses air ... to keep) is moderate, and other 'to's are weak. It also fires on Turkish or Hungarian instrumental markers ('ile', '-al'), which mean 'with/by means of'.

Fires on a sentence boundary or the first word of a new sentence or paragraph, especially the period or '.\n\n' ending an expository statement and a sentence-initial imperative or participle ('Read', 'Show', 'Based', 'Support', 'Expand', 'Please'). Mid-sentence tokens fire weakly.

Fires on the period (or '?', '!') ending a short, informal, opinionated or conversational sentence in blogs, forum comments or rants ('I won't be your patsy.', 'Glad to see Bruce Eckel involved.'). Periods in formal scientific prose fire only weakly or moderately.

Fires mainly on the quantifier 'all' (and related words 'any', 'such', 'each', 'a') in quantifying positions ('which all occurred', 'were all lower', 'all across the country', 'unlike any other'), including the 'all' piece of 'alligator' and 'allodynia'. It also fires on subword pieces in Cyrillic, Hungarian or Albanian text.

Fires on words that state an extent, span or range: 'to' in 'from 1938 to 1970', 'covered/covers the area', 'ended on', 'consisting of', and the last digit of a year range (2012-2015). It also fires on layout size values in code or markup ('match_parent', 'row-fluid', '400px', 'type: Array').
